name: Tobruk siege opening: 12 April–4 May 1941 (linked research)

aim.cw: Hold Tobruk and deny the Axis its harbour while the frontier defences are prepared.
aim.axis: Take Tobruk and its harbour before the Commonwealth can consolidate the frontier.

about: Linked research chapter covering 12 April–4 May 1941. It retains the actual played 11 April map, units, losses and stocks, including a possible Axis-held Tobruk. The Easter Battle on 13–14 April and Battle of the Salient from 30 April to 4 May are dated by the Australian War Memorial. The current 10 km map and generic combat model do not represent Tobruk perimeter posts, tank serviceability or the detailed attacks. The Axis order to take Tobruk is a broad operational aim, not a claim that the historical attackers reached the port. Copied owners and placements are structural placeholders, not a separately verified start.

sources.W: Wavell, Western Desert operations despatch, London Gazette 37628, sections 10–21: plan, forces, opening, Nibeiwa and Sidi Barrani
sources.P: Playfair et al., The Mediterranean and Middle East, vol. I, chapter XIV: positions, supply preparation, assault sequence and withdrawal of 4th Indian Division
sources.A: Australian official history, To Benghazi, chapter 6: Commonwealth formations and armoured screening task
sources.E: Game estimate: individual-unit strength, exact 10 km placement, opening stock or supply setting not verified by the cited account
sources.B: Australian official history, To Benghazi, chapter VII Before Bardia: 16th Brigade via Buq Buq and Sollum 17-19 December; 17th Brigade and divisional HQ move ordered for 22 December; 19th Brigade forward 1 January
sources.P2: Playfair et al., The Mediterranean and Middle East, vol. I, chapter XV: Sollum port and supply, Bardia perimeter preparations, ammunition delay and 7th RTR serviceability
sources.O: 6th Australian Division operation order, 1 January 1941, Appendix 2 of Australian official history To Benghazi: western attack, phases, 7th RTR and 17th Brigade
sources.H: Australian War Memorial Battle of Bardia: breach 3 January, town 4 January, southern surrender 5 January
sources.T: Australian official history, To Benghazi, chapter 9: XXII Corps, 61st Sirte and Tobruk garrison; approximately 25,000 men and 220 guns estimated 15 January
sources.T2: Australian official history, To Benghazi, chapter 9: Bardia to Tobruk, XXII Corps garrison, preparation and attack on 21 January
sources.P3: UK official history, The Mediterranean and Middle East vol I chapter XV: Tobruk garrison, routes, preparations and fall
sources.D: Australian official history, To Benghazi, chapter 10, The Engagement at Derna: 22 January advance, Derna rearguard and 30 January occupation; contemporary estimate of 60th Sabratha and Babini armour near Derna/Mechili. Exact strength and scenario-entry placement remain unverified.
sources.F: Australian official history, To Benghazi, chapter 11, Beda Fomm and Benghazi: 3 February withdrawal, 4 February desert march, 5–7 February road block and surrender, and the Benghazi occupation.
sources.R: Playfair et al., The Mediterranean and Middle East, volume II, chapter I: defence of Cyrenaica, 7th Armoured refit, 6th/9th Australian relief, 2nd Armoured weakness, German arrivals, 24 March El Agheila and 31 March Mersa Brega attack.
sources.W2: Australian War Memorial, Tobruk diaries timeline: 8–9 March 9th Australian relief of 6th, 31 March Axis attack and 10–11 April siege onset.
sources.R2: Playfair et al., The Mediterranean and Middle East, volume II, chapter II, The Loss of Cyrenaica: 31 March Mersa Brega defence, 1 April German occupation, 4 April Benghazi entry, 6–7 April withdrawal and Mechili actions, and 18th Australian Brigade arrival at Tobruk by 7 April.
sources.S: Australian War Memorial, Tobruk diaries timeline: Easter Battle 13–14 April and Battle of the Salient 30 April–4 May; Battles for Tobruk: 9th Division ordered to hold the harbour and delay Axis advance while frontier defences were prepared.
